title: Major sins
intro: Sins Allah clearly forbade in the Qur’an, with punishment in this world and the next.

learn.html: A major sin is anything Allah clearly forbade in the Qur’an, with a punishment in this world and the next.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your smaller misdeeds. <small>(Qur’an, An-Nisa’ 4:31)</small>

items: Taking a life – including one’s own. Allah gives life, and only He has the right to take it.
Leaving Salah – Allah warns about those who abandoned prayer and followed their desires, except those who repent, believe and do good. (Qur’an, Maryam 19:59–60)
Not doing the Islamic duties of fasting, zakah and Hajj – they are fard.
Disobeying parents – the Prophet (SAW) said: “Allah’s pleasure is in the parents’ pleasure, and Allah’s anger is in the parents’ anger.” (Tirmidhi)
Cutting family ties – “Whoever cuts family ties will not enter Jannah.” (Bukhari)
Zina and everything that leads to it, like indecent looking and indecent talk.
Using up an orphan’s wealth and treating orphans unjustly.
Lying – it leads to evil and harms people and the community.
Gambling, games of chance, horoscopes and betting – people see some small gain, but the harm is far greater.
Alcohol – every drink with alcohol, in any amount, is forbidden. “Alcohol is the mother of all evils.” (Hakim)

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Because of the harm they do, Allah forbade the major sins – and it is our duty to warn others, to call to good and turn people away from evil.

practice.title: Major sins
practice.prompt: Tap every major sin from the lesson, then tap Check.

options: Something Allah clearly forbade, with punishment in both worlds

prompts: 🗣️ How would you talk to someone who commits major sins? What would help them understand the harm and stop? Should we speak gently or harshly?
